summary: One POST form with a user name and a password in the sign-in panel of /main.html, on the connection's own origin. The page carries an invisible reCAPTCHA, and the operator's conditions say a code sent by SMS follows the password.

sources.title: The public My Vodafone entry, rendered once without an account
sources.note: The entry address forwards to /main.html on the catalog host itself; no other host served the page. The sign-in panel is in the top document, inside the header menu, and was rendered. The other frames are empty or belong to reCAPTCHA; none holds a sign-in control.

sources.title: Vodafone Portugal: conditions of the My Vodafone service
sources.note: States that a second factor applies to both ways of signing in: with the registration credentials, the password and then a verification code sent by SMS; with the customer's own Vodafone number, a code by SMS and a PIN. It forbids reproducing the service's content without permission; it has no clause on automated access. No markup.

fixtures.note: In the capture the submit button is disabled until the fields have a value. The fixture has no script, so it leaves the disabled attribute out. The hidden recovery form is kept because its input shares the name of the user-name field.

staysInteractive.note: The capture has a reCAPTCHA frame and response field, neither displayed: an invisible reCAPTCHA. A challenge can appear when the form is submitted.
Per the operator's conditions: a verification code sent by SMS after the password. The page that asks for it was not observed.
A cookie dialog (div#cookiesModal) is part of the page. It is not answered by the steps.
Signing in with the customer's own Vodafone number (code by SMS and a PIN) is a different path and is not automated.

unverified: The page can change at any time. This is one anonymous render on the review date.
Nothing after the submit was observed, because no account was used: the reCAPTCHA outcome and the SMS code page.

What the page's script does on submit. The form declares the method post and no action, and the reCAPTCHA response field is outside the form, so a script very likely takes part; automatic sign-in clicks the form's own submit button.
That the submit button becomes enabled when the application types into the two fields.
That the sign-in panel is in view without opening the header menu. The capture reports the form as rendered, which says it has a layout box, not that it is on screen.

Whether another host ever takes over the password step. The in-repository review of 2026-10-06 (docs/portugal-portal-profiles.md) mentions authorisation addresses on login.vodafone.pt; the capture shows the form on my.vodafone.pt, and nothing is typed anywhere else.
neededFromUser: One sign-in with this layout, or the sign-in panel and the code page that follows it saved as "Webpage, Complete". Save any page signed out and with no password typed in; keep the "_files" folder beside the .html and both outside the repository: they can hold the account name.
notes: Checked before the capture: robots.txt of my.vodafone.pt disallows /LOGIN and /LOGOUT but neither the entry address nor /main.html, where the form is, and the service conditions have no clause on automated access. Only the catalog entry address was loaded, once, with no input.
